en.title: Appendix M.4: merging first-order AND/OR effects
en.overview: The singleton activation events coincide, so merging preserves their contribution on every mask.

definitions.body_md: Fix the finite universe $N=\{1,\ldots,n\}$, input $x$, input baseline vector $r$, and a real-valued model $v$. The mask $x_U$ retains coordinates in $U$ and sets the others to $r$; write $g(U)=v(x_U)$ and output baseline $b=g(\varnothing)$. The source input baseline $b_i$ is distinct from this scalar $b$. Choose one decomposition function $\gamma$ and put $a(U)=g(U)/2+\gamma_U$, $o(U)=g(U)/2-\gamma_U$, so that $a+o=g$. The AND component dividend is $A(S)=\sum_{U\subseteq S}(-1)^{|S|-|U|}a(U)$; the nonempty OR component dividend is $O(S)=-\sum_{U\subseteq S}(-1)^{|S|-|U|}o(N\setminus U)$. The raw total-output dividend $I_g$ and component dividend $A$ remain distinct. Local $a=g_{and}$, $o=g_{or}$, $A=I_{g_{and}}$, and $O=O_{g_{or}}$ abbreviate the corresponding public concepts.

proof_steps.title: Check the singleton activation events
proof_steps.body_md: For every $T\subseteq N$, $\{i\}\subseteq T$ if and only if $i\in T$, and $\{i\}\cap T\ne\varnothing$ also if and only if $i\in T$. The activation indicators coincide.

proof_steps.title: Merge the coefficients and explain the representation change
proof_steps.body_md: Adding the two coefficients under their common indicator proves the claim, including coefficients of either sign. This changes the AND/OR representation and may change singleton saliency counts, but preserves the singleton’s total contribution on every mask. Containment and intersection differ for larger coalitions, so this merge cannot be generalized to all orders.

# Appendix C. Proof of Theorem 2 (main Theorem 3.2)

Source: official PDF pages 12–14. This is a complete mathematical transcription of the author calculation. In this transcription U denotes the background called S in the PDF, and the source's A and B marginal components are written A_U and B_U. The source interaction names Iand and Ior are preserved. These changes only prevent a bound-variable collision; the erroneous nonempty-intersection domains on page 14 are retained below.

According to the definition of Shapley values,
\[
\varphi(i)=\sum_{U\subseteq N\setminus\{i\}}\frac{|U|!(n-|U|-1)!}{n!}[v(U\cup\{i\})-v(U)]
=\mathbb E_{U\subseteq N\setminus\{i\}}[v(U\cup\{i\})-v(U)].
\]
According to Eq. (10), for every U⊆N,
\[
v(U)=v(\varnothing)+\sum_{L\subseteq U,L\ne\varnothing}I_{and}(L)+\sum_{L\cap U\ne\varnothing}I_{or}(L).
\]
Thus
\[
\begin{aligned}
v(U\cup\{i\})-v(U)
&=\left[v(\varnothing)+\sum_{L\subseteq U\cup\{i\},L\ne\varnothing}I_{and}(L)+\sum_{L\cap(U\cup\{i\})\ne\varnothing}I_{or}(L)\right]\\
&\quad-\left[v(\varnothing)+\sum_{L\subseteq U,L\ne\varnothing}I_{and}(L)+\sum_{L\cap U\ne\varnothing}I_{or}(L)\right]\\
&=\left[\sum_{L\subseteq U\cup\{i\},L\ne\varnothing}I_{and}(L)-\sum_{L\subseteq U,L\ne\varnothing}I_{and}(L)\right]
+\left[\sum_{L\cap(U\cup\{i\})\ne\varnothing}I_{or}(L)-\sum_{L\cap U\ne\varnothing}I_{or}(L)\right]\\
&=\underbrace{\sum_{L\subseteq U}I_{and}(L\cup\{i\})}_{A_U}
+\underbrace{\sum_{L\cap U=\varnothing}I_{or}(L\cup\{i\})}_{B_U}.
\end{aligned}
\]
This breaks the Shapley value into E[A_U+B_U]. For the AND part the complete page-13 chain is
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E_U[A_U]
&=\mathbb E_U\sum_{L\subseteq U}I_{and}(L\cup\{i\})\\
&=\frac1n\sum_{m=0}^{n-1}\frac1{\binom{n-1}m}\sum_{\substack{U\subseteq N\setminus\{i\}\\|U|=m}}\sum_{L\subseteq U}I_{and}(L\cup\{i\})\\
&=\frac1n\sum_{L\subseteq N\setminus\{i\}}\sum_{m=0}^{n-1}\frac1{\binom{n-1}m}\sum_{\substack{U\supseteq L,\ U\subseteq N\setminus\{i\}\\|U|=m}}I_{and}(L\cup\{i\})\\
&=\frac1n\sum_{L\subseteq N\setminus\{i\}}\sum_{m=|L|}^{n-1}\frac1{\binom{n-1}m}\sum_{\substack{U\supseteq L,\ U\subseteq N\setminus\{i\}\\|U|=m}}I_{and}(L\cup\{i\})\\
&=\frac1n\sum_{L\subseteq N\setminus\{i\}}\sum_{m=|L|}^{n-1}\frac{\binom{n-1-|L|}{m-|L|}}{\binom{n-1}m}I_{and}(L\cup\{i\})\\
&=\sum_{L\subseteq N\setminus\{i\}}\underbrace{\left[\frac1n\sum_{k=0}^{n-1-|L|}\frac{\binom{n-1-|L|}k}{\binom{n-1}{|L|+k}}\right]}_{\alpha_L}I_{and}(L\cup\{i\})\\
&=\sum_{L\subseteq N\setminus\{i\}}\frac1{|L|+1}I_{and}(L\cup\{i\})
=\sum_{T\subseteq N,i\in T}\frac1{|T|}I_{and}(T).
\end{aligned}
\]
The source comments give |U|≥|L| in the third-to-fourth line, k=m−|L| in the sixth line, and T=L∪{i} in the last line.

The OR chain on page 14 prints the following domains. **The first three nonempty-intersection conditions are source errors and are not corrected in this original-proof field.**
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E_U[B_U]
&=\mathbb E_U\sum_{L\cap U\ne\varnothing}I_{or}(L\cup\{i\})\\
&=\frac1n\sum_{m=0}^{n-1}\frac1{\binom{n-1}m}\sum_{\substack{U\subseteq N\setminus\{i\}\\|U|=m}}\sum_{L\cap U\ne\varnothing}I_{or}(L\cup\{i\})\\
&=\frac1n\sum_{L\subseteq N\setminus\{i\}}\sum_{m=0}^{n-1}\frac1{\binom{n-1}m}\sum_{\substack{U\cap L\ne\varnothing,\ U\subseteq N\setminus\{i\}\\|U|=m}}I_{or}(L\cup\{i\})\\
&=\frac1n\sum_{L\subseteq N\setminus\{i\}}\sum_{m=0}^{n-1}\frac1{\binom{n-1}m}\sum_{\substack{U\subseteq N\setminus\{i\}\setminus L\\|U|=m}}I_{or}(L\cup\{i\})\\
&=\frac1n\sum_{L\subseteq N\setminus\{i\}}\sum_{m=0}^{n-1-|L|}\frac1{\binom{n-1}m}\sum_{\substack{U\subseteq N\setminus\{i\}\setminus L\\|U|=m}}I_{or}(L\cup\{i\})\\
&=\frac1n\sum_{L\subseteq N\setminus\{i\}}\sum_{m=0}^{n-1-|L|}\frac{\binom{n-1-|L|}m}{\binom{n-1}m}I_{or}(L\cup\{i\})\\
&=\frac1n\sum_{L\subseteq N\setminus\{i\}}\sum_{k=0}^{n-1-|L|}\frac{\binom{n-1-|L|}{n-1-|L|-k}}{\binom{n-1}{n-1-|L|-k}}I_{or}(L\cup\{i\})\\
&=\frac1n\sum_{L\subseteq N\setminus\{i\}}\sum_{k=0}^{n-1-|L|}\frac{\binom{n-1-|L|}k}{\binom{n-1}{|L|+k}}I_{or}(L\cup\{i\})\\
&=\frac1n\sum_{L\subseteq N\setminus\{i\}}\frac n{|L|+1}I_{or}(L\cup\{i\})\\
&=\sum_{L\subseteq N\setminus\{i\}}\frac1{|L|+1}I_{or}(L\cup\{i\})
=\sum_{T\subseteq N,i\in T}\frac1{|T|}I_{or}(T).
\end{aligned}
\]
The source comments use |U|≤n−1−|L| and k=n−1−|L|−m. Adding both parts concludes
\[
\varphi(i)=\mathbb E_U[A_U]+\mathbb E_U[B_U]
=\sum_{T\subseteq N,i\in T}\frac1{|T|}[I_{and}(T)+I_{or}(T)].
\]

en.overview: First/last positions in a permutation give the same equal-share weight for OR and AND effects.
assumptions: $N$ is finite. Fix the same input, model, and input baseline. The raw output baseline need not be zero.

definitions.body_md: Fix a finite universe $N$, input $x$, and input baseline vector $r$; put $g(U)=v(x_U)$ and $b=g(\varnothing)$. Local $a=g_{and}$ and $o=g_{or}$ abbreviate the two source components, $a(U)=g(U)/2+\gamma_U$ and $o(U)=g(U)/2-\gamma_U$. proof_steps.title: Expand masked marginals
proof_steps.body_md: Subtract Eq. (10) at U and U∪{i}. An AND term remains exactly when it contains i and its other members lie in U. An OR term remains exactly when it contains i and its other members are disjoint from U. The baseline cancels.

lean_refs.explanation_md: This declaration verifies the reconstruction identity used here. Subtraction and activation-set splitting are expanded in prose and are not a separate formalized marginal-step theorem.

proof_steps.title: Count first and last positions
proof_steps.body_md: Let $n=|N|$ and explicitly define $w(U)=|U|!(n-|U|-1)!/n!$ for $U\subseteq N\setminus\{i\}$. This is the probability that U is exactly the predecessor set of i in a uniformly random permutation: the predecessor and successor orders have $|U|!$ and $(n-|U|-1)!$ choices among $n!$ permutations. For fixed nonempty $T\subseteq N$ containing i, its AND term occurs exactly when i is last in T, and its OR term exactly when i is first. Relabeling the members partitions all permutations into $|T|$ equally sized classes, so each probability is $1/|T|$. Lean verifies these weights by an equivalent finite factorial-convolution route; the individual permutation-language sentences are not separately formalized.

lean_refs.explanation_md: The Lean route proves the AND kernel by finite factorial convolution and obtains the OR kernel by complement reindexing. The permutation count here is the independent readable argument.

proof_steps.title: Exchange finite sums and check the domain
proof_steps.body_md: Interchange the finite sums and accumulate the AND and OR coefficients for each T. Membership $i\in N$ implies $n\ge1$, and every contributing T contains i, so its denominator is nonzero. No zero baseline or particular γ-selection rule is needed. # Appendix D. Proof of Theorem 3 (main Theorem 3.3)

Source: official PDF pages 14–15. The original names v_and,v_or and original alternating exponents are retained. The displayed exponent +1 differs by two from the common paired form −1, so it is not itself a sign error.

According to the AND/OR definitions,
\[
\begin{aligned}
I_{and}(S)&=\sum_{L\subseteq S}(-1)^{|S|-|L|}v_{and}(L)
=\sum_{L\subseteq S\setminus\{i\}}(-1)^{|S|-|L|+1}[v_{and}(L\cup\{i\})-v_{and}(L)],\\
I_{or}(S)&=-\sum_{L\subseteq S}(-1)^{|S|-|L|}v_{or}(N\setminus L)
=\sum_{L\subseteq S\setminus\{i\}}(-1)^{|S|-|L|+1}[v_{or}(N\setminus L)-v_{or}(N\setminus L\setminus\{i\})],
\end{aligned}
\]
where v(L)=v_and(L)+v_or(L). Define, solely to keep the long source braces readable,
\[
D(L)=[v_{and}(L\cup\{i\})-v_{and}(L)]+[v_{or}(N\setminus L)-v_{or}(N\setminus L\setminus\{i\})].
\]
The source page-15 chain, with each repeated brace D(L) written in this explicitly defined shorthand, is
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{S\subseteq N,S\ni i}\frac{I_{and}(S)+I_{or}(S)}{2^{|S|-1}}
&=\sum_{S\subseteq N,S\ni i}\sum_{L\subseteq S\setminus\{i\}}\frac{(-1)^{|S|-|L|+1}}{2^{|S|-1}}D(L)\\
&=\sum_{S\subseteq N\setminus\{i\}}\sum_{L\subseteq S}\frac{(-1)^{|S|-|L|}}{2^{|S|}}D(L)\\
&=\sum_{L\subseteq N\setminus\{i\}}(-1)^{|L|}\sum_{\substack{S\subseteq N\setminus\{i\}\\S\supseteq L}}\frac{(-1)^{|S|}}{2^{|S|}}D(L)\\
&=\sum_{L\subseteq N\setminus\{i\}}(-1)^{|L|}\frac{(-1)^{|L|}}{2^{|N|-1}}D(L)\\
&=\sum_{L\subseteq N\setminus\{i\}}\frac1{2^{|N|-1}}D(L)\\
&=\sum_{S\subseteq N\setminus\{i\}}\frac{v_{and}(S\cup\{i\})-v_{and}(S)}{2^{|N|-1}}
+\sum_{S\subseteq N\setminus\{i\}}\frac{v_{or}(N\setminus S)-v_{or}(N\setminus S\setminus\{i\})}{2^{|N|-1}}\\
&=\sum_{S\subseteq N\setminus\{i\}}\frac{v_{and}(S\cup\{i\})-v_{and}(S)}{2^{|N|-1}}
+\sum_{S\subseteq N\setminus\{i\}}\frac{v_{or}(S\cup\{i\})-v_{or}(S)}{2^{|N|-1}}\\
&=\sum_{S\subseteq N\setminus\{i\}}\frac{[v_{and}(S\cup\{i\})+v_{or}(S\cup\{i\})]-[v_{and}(S)+v_{or}(S)]}{2^{|N|-1}}\\
&=\sum_{S\subseteq N\setminus\{i\}}\frac{v(S\cup\{i\})-v(S)}{2^{|N|-1}}=B(i).
\end{aligned}
\]
The source comment in the fourth line asserts
\[
\sum_{\substack{S\subseteq N\setminus\{i\}\\S\supseteq L}}\frac{(-1)^{|S|}}{2^{|S|}}=\frac{(-1)^{|L|}}{2^{|N|-1}}.
\]
The last line gives the claimed reformulation.

# Appendix E. Proof of Theorem 4 and Corollary 5

Source: official PDF pages 15–16. Main labels: Theorem 3.4 and Corollary 3.5. Put J(T)=I_and(T)+I_or(T) only as a shorthand for the exact repeated source bracket.

According to Theorem 2, φ_i=varphi(i)=∑_{T⊆N,i∈T}J(T)/|T|. According to Eq. (6), φ(S)=∑_{T⊇S}|S|J(T)/|T|. The complete calculation is
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{i\in S}\varphi(i)
&=\sum_{i\in S}\sum_{T\subseteq N,T\ni i}\frac1{|T|}J(T)\\
&=\sum_{i\in S}\left[\sum_{T\subseteq N,T\supseteq S}\frac1{|T|}J(T)+\sum_{T\subseteq N,T\not\supseteq S,T\ni i}\frac1{|T|}J(T)\right]\\
&=\sum_{i\in S}\left[\frac1{|S|}\sum_{T\subseteq N,T\supseteq S}\frac{|S|}{|T|}J(T)+\sum_{T\subseteq N,T\not\supseteq S,T\ni i}\frac1{|T|}J(T)\right]\\
&=\sum_{i\in S}\left[\frac1{|S|}\phi(S)+\sum_{T\subseteq N,T\not\supseteq S,T\ni i}\frac1{|T|}J(T)\right]\\
&=\sum_{i\in S}\frac1{|S|}\phi(S)+\sum_{i\in S}\sum_{T\subseteq N,T\not\supseteq S,T\ni i}\frac1{|T|}J(T)\\
&=|S|\frac1{|S|}\phi(S)+\sum_{\substack{T\subseteq N\\T\cap S\ne\varnothing,\ T\cap S\ne S}}\frac{|T\cap S|}{|T|}J(T)\\
&=\phi(S)+\sum_{\substack{T\subseteq N\\T\cap S\ne\varnothing,\ T\cap S\ne S}}\frac{|T\cap S|}{|T|}J(T).
\end{aligned}
\]
The source explains that each J(T)/|T| is counted |T∩S| times. It does not discuss S=empty.

For Corollary 5 the original printed premise is
\[
\forall T\in\{T:S\not\subseteq T,\ T\subseteq N,\ i\in S\},\quad I_{and}(T)=I_{or}(T)=0.
\]
The free i is retained as printed. The source then obtains
\[
\sum_{i\in S}\varphi(i)=\phi(S)+\sum_{\substack{T\subseteq N\\T\cap S\ne\varnothing,\ T\cap S\ne S}}\frac{|T\cap S|}{|T|}J(T)=\phi(S),
\]
and, for the individual variable,
\[
\varphi(i)=\frac1{|S|}\phi(S)+\sum_{T\subseteq N,T\not\supseteq S,T\ni i}\frac1{|T|}J(T)=\frac1{|S|}\phi(S).
\]
This concludes both source results.

# Appendix E. Proof of Theorem 4 and Corollary 5

Source: official PDF pages 15–16. Main labels: Theorem 3.4 and Corollary 3.5. Put J(T)=I_and(T)+I_or(T) only as a shorthand for the exact repeated source bracket.

According to Theorem 2, φ_i=varphi(i)=∑_{T⊆N,i∈T}J(T)/|T|. According to Eq. (6), φ(S)=∑_{T⊇S}|S|J(T)/|T|. The complete calculation is
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{i\in S}\varphi(i)
&=\sum_{i\in S}\sum_{T\subseteq N,T\ni i}\frac1{|T|}J(T)\\
&=\sum_{i\in S}\left[\sum_{T\subseteq N,T\supseteq S}\frac1{|T|}J(T)+\sum_{T\subseteq N,T\not\supseteq S,T\ni i}\frac1{|T|}J(T)\right]\\
&=\sum_{i\in S}\left[\frac1{|S|}\sum_{T\subseteq N,T\supseteq S}\frac{|S|}{|T|}J(T)+\sum_{T\subseteq N,T\not\supseteq S,T\ni i}\frac1{|T|}J(T)\right]\\
&=\sum_{i\in S}\left[\frac1{|S|}\phi(S)+\sum_{T\subseteq N,T\not\supseteq S,T\ni i}\frac1{|T|}J(T)\right]\\
&=\sum_{i\in S}\frac1{|S|}\phi(S)+\sum_{i\in S}\sum_{T\subseteq N,T\not\supseteq S,T\ni i}\frac1{|T|}J(T)\\
&=|S|\frac1{|S|}\phi(S)+\sum_{\substack{T\subseteq N\\T\cap S\ne\varnothing,\ T\cap S\ne S}}\frac{|T\cap S|}{|T|}J(T)\\
&=\phi(S)+\sum_{\substack{T\subseteq N\\T\cap S\ne\varnothing,\ T\cap S\ne S}}\frac{|T\cap S|}{|T|}J(T).
\end{aligned}
\]
The source explains that each J(T)/|T| is counted |T∩S| times. It does not discuss S=empty.

For Corollary 5 the original printed premise is
\[
\forall T\in\{T:S\not\subseteq T,\ T\subseteq N,\ i\in S\},\quad I_{and}(T)=I_{or}(T)=0.
\]
The free i is retained as printed. The source then obtains
\[
\sum_{i\in S}\varphi(i)=\phi(S)+\sum_{\substack{T\subseteq N\\T\cap S\ne\varnothing,\ T\cap S\ne S}}\frac{|T\cap S|}{|T|}J(T)=\phi(S),
\]
and, for the individual variable,
\[
\varphi(i)=\frac1{|S|}\phi(S)+\sum_{T\subseteq N,T\not\supseteq S,T\ni i}\frac1{|T|}J(T)=\frac1{|S|}\phi(S).
\]
This concludes both source results.

# Appendix F. Proof of Theorem 6 and Corollary 7

Source: official PDF pages 16–17. Main labels: Theorem 3.6 and Corollary 3.7. J(T)=I_and(T)+I_or(T) is a shorthand for the repeated source bracket.

\[

\varphi(i)
&=\sum_{T\subseteq N,T\ni i}\frac1{|T|}J(T)\\

&=\frac1{|S|}\phi(S)+\sum_{T\subseteq N,T\not\supseteq S,T\ni i}\frac1{|T|}J(T).
\end{aligned}
\]

\[
\begin{aligned}

\end{aligned}

# Appendix G.1. Proof of Anonymity

Source: official PDF page 17. Original proof inference about the two components is retained.

The source lists
\[
\begin{aligned}
I_{and,v}(T)&=\sum_{L\subseteq T}(-1)^{|T|-|L|}v_{and}(L),&I_{or,v}(T)&=-\sum_{L\subseteq T}(-1)^{|T|-|L|}v_{or}(N\setminus L),\\
I_{and,\sigma v}(\sigma T)&=\sum_{L\subseteq\sigma T}(-1)^{|\sigma T|-|L|}(\sigma v_{and})(L),&
I_{or,\sigma v}(\sigma T)&=-\sum_{L\subseteq\sigma T}(-1)^{|\sigma T|-|L|}(\sigma v_{or})(N\setminus L).
\end{aligned}
\]
It claims that σv(σS)=v(S) implies σv_and(σS)=v_and(S) and σv_or(σS)=v_or(S). Its two complete change-of-variable chains are
\[
\begin{aligned}
I_{and,\sigma v}(\sigma T)
&=\sum_{L\subseteq\sigma T}(-1)^{|\sigma T|-|L|}(\sigma v_{and})(L)\\
&=\sum_{L=\sigma K\subseteq\sigma T}(-1)^{|\sigma T|-|\sigma K|}(\sigma v_{and})(\sigma K)\\
&=\sum_{L=\sigma K\subseteq\sigma T}(-1)^{|T|-|K|}v_{and}(K)
=\sum_{K\subseteq T}(-1)^{|T|-|K|}v_{and}(K)=I_{and,v}(T),\\
I_{or,\sigma v}(\sigma T)
&=-\sum_{L\subseteq\sigma T}(-1)^{|\sigma T|-|L|}(\sigma v_{or})(N\setminus L)\\
&=-\sum_{L=\sigma K\subseteq\sigma T}(-1)^{|\sigma T|-|\sigma K|}(\sigma v_{or})(N\setminus\sigma K)\\
&=-\sum_{L=\sigma K\subseteq\sigma T}(-1)^{|\sigma T|-|\sigma K|}(\sigma v_{or})(\sigma(N\setminus K))\\
&=-\sum_{L=\sigma K\subseteq\sigma T}(-1)^{|T|-|K|}v_{or}(N\setminus K)
=-\sum_{K\subseteq T}(-1)^{|T|-|K|}v_{or}(N\setminus K)=I_{or,v}(T).
\end{aligned}
\]
With J_v(T)=I_and,v(T)+I_or,v(T), Eq.(6) then gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\phi_{\sigma v}(\sigma S)
&=\sum_{T\supseteq\sigma S}\frac{|\sigma S|}{|T|}J_{\sigma v}(T)\\
&=\sum_{T=\sigma L\supseteq\sigma S}\frac{|\sigma S|}{|\sigma L|}[I_{and,\sigma v}(\sigma L)+I_{or,\sigma v}(\sigma L)]\\
&=\sum_{T=\sigma L\supseteq\sigma S}\frac{|S|}{|L|}[I_{and,v}(L)+I_{or,v}(L)]\\
&=\sum_{L\supseteq S}\frac{|S|}{|L|}[I_{and,v}(L)+I_{or,v}(L)]=\phi_v(S).
\end{aligned}
\]

It then claims that equality v(U∪{i})=v(U∪{j}) for all U⊆N\{i,j} gives the same equalities for v_and and v_or. The full interaction-difference chains are
\[
\begin{aligned}
I_{and}(T\cup\{i\})-I_{and}(T\cup\{j\})
&=\sum_{L\subseteq T\cup\{i\}}(-1)^{|T\cup\{i\}|-|L|}v_{and}(L)-\sum_{L\subseteq T\cup\{j\}}(-1)^{|T\cup\{j\}|-|L|}v_{and}(L)\\
&=\left[\sum_{L\subseteq T}(-1)^{|T\cup\{i\}|-|L|}v_{and}(L)+\sum_{L\subseteq T}(-1)^{|T\cup\{i\}|-|L\cup\{i\}|}v_{and}(L\cup\{i\})\right]\\
&\quad-\left[\sum_{L\subseteq T}(-1)^{|T\cup\{j\}|-|L|}v_{and}(L)+\sum_{L\subseteq T}(-1)^{|T\cup\{j\}|-|L\cup\{j\}|}v_{and}(L\cup\{j\})\right]\\
&=\sum_{L\subseteq T}(-1)^{|T|-|L|}[v_{and}(L\cup\{i\})-v_{and}(L\cup\{j\})]=0,\\
I_{or}(T\cup\{i\})-I_{or}(T\cup\{j\})
&=-\sum_{L\subseteq T\cup\{i\}}(-1)^{|T\cup\{i\}|-|L|}v_{or}(N\setminus L)+\sum_{L\subseteq T\cup\{j\}}(-1)^{|T\cup\{j\}|-|L|}v_{or}(N\setminus L)\\
&=\left[\sum_{L\subseteq T}(-1)^{|T\cup\{j\}|-|L|}v_{or}(N\setminus L)+\sum_{L\subseteq T}(-1)^{|T\cup\{j\}|-|L\cup\{j\}|}v_{or}(N\setminus(L\cup\{j\}))\right]\\
&\quad-\left[\sum_{L\subseteq T}(-1)^{|T\cup\{i\}|-|L|}v_{or}(N\setminus L)+\sum_{L\subseteq T}(-1)^{|T\cup\{i\}|-|L\cup\{i\}|}v_{or}(N\setminus(L\cup\{i\}))\right]\\
&=\sum_{L\subseteq T}(-1)^{|T|-|L|}[v_{or}((N\setminus(L\cup\{i,j\}))\cup\{i\})-v_{or}((N\setminus(L\cup\{i,j\}))\cup\{j\})]=0.
\end{aligned}
\]
Let J(T)=I_and(T)+I_or(T). The complete attribution-difference chain is
\[
\begin{aligned}
\phi(S\cup\{i\})-\phi(S\cup\{j\})
&=\sum_{T\supseteq S\cup\{i\}}\frac{|S\cup\{i\}|}{|T|}J(T)-\sum_{T\supseteq S\cup\{j\}}\frac{|S\cup\{j\}|}{|T|}J(T)\\
&=\left[\sum_{T\supseteq S\cup\{i,j\}}\frac{|S|+1}{|T|}J(T)+\sum_{T\supseteq S\cup\{i\},j\notin T}\frac{|S|+1}{|T|}J(T)\right]\\
&\quad-\left[\sum_{T\supseteq S\cup\{i,j\}}\frac{|S|+1}{|T|}J(T)+\sum_{T\supseteq S\cup\{j\},i\notin T}\frac{|S|+1}{|T|}J(T)\right]\\
&=\sum_{T\supseteq S\cup\{i\},j\notin T}\frac{|S|+1}{|T|}J(T)-\sum_{T\supseteq S\cup\{j\},i\notin T}\frac{|S|+1}{|T|}J(T)\\
&=\sum_{\substack{T\supseteq S\\T\subseteq N\setminus\{i,j\}}}\frac{|S|+1}{|T\cup\{i\}|}J(T\cup\{i\})-\sum_{\substack{T\supseteq S\\T\subseteq N\setminus\{i,j\}}}\frac{|S|+1}{|T\cup\{j\}|}J(T\cup\{j\})\\

\end{aligned}
\]

definitions.body_md: Fix a finite universe $N$, input $x$, and input baseline vector $r$; put $g(U)=v(x_U)$ and $b=g(\varnothing)$. Local $a=g_{and}$ and $o=g_{or}$ abbreviate the two source components, $a(U)=g(U)/2+\gamma_U$ and $o(U)=g(U)/2-\gamma_U$. Local $A=I_{g_{and}}$ and $O=O_{g_{or}}$ abbreviate the AND component’s Möbius dividend and the nonempty OR negative complementary dividend; $J=A+O$. The raw output baseline need not vanish.
For a nonempty coalition $S$, Eq.(6) is $\phi(S)=\sum_{T\subseteq N,S\subseteq T}|S|J(T)/|T|$. The source empty-coalition term contains $0/0$; no new value convention is inserted here.

proof_steps.title: Construct a decomposition satisfying the source definitions
proof_steps.body_md: Let $N=\{1,2,3\}$, $g(U)=|U|$, and $P=\{1,3\}$. Define $a(U)=\mathbf1[P\subseteq U]+\mathbf1[2\in U]$ and $o(U)=\mathbf1[U\cap P\ne\varnothing]$. Checking 0, 1, and 2 present members of P gives $a+o=g$. The actual source parameter is $\gamma_U=a(U)-g(U)/2$.

proof_steps.title: Check coefficients and global optimality
proof_steps.body_md: Pure AND/OR coefficient distribution gives $A(P)=O(P)=1$ and $A(\{2\})=1$, with all other nonempty coefficients zero. Thus L1=3. proof_steps.title: Compute attributions and test the original conclusion
proof_steps.body_md: The attributions are $\phi(\{1,3\})=2$ and $\phi(\{2,3\})=0$. The cardinality game satisfies every premise of α with $i=1,j=2,L=\{3\}$, and of β with $S=\{1\},T=\{2\},L=\{3\}$, but their conclusions fail. For anonymity, independently selecting an optimum after permuting only the total game need not preserve attribution; transporting the fixed components does give the original valid change-of-variables identity. These scopes are distinct.

# Appendix G.2. Proof of Symmetry α

Source: official PDF pages 18–19. The unsupported transfer of total-game symmetry to each component is retained.

The source defines, for k=i,j,
\[
I_{and}(T\cup\{k\})=\sum_{L\subseteq T\cup\{k\}}(-1)^{|T\cup\{k\}|-|L|}v_{and}(L),\quad
I_{or}(T\cup\{k\})=-\sum_{L\subseteq T\cup\{k\}}(-1)^{|T\cup\{k\}|-|L|}v_{or}(N\setminus L).
\]
It then claims that equality v(U∪{i})=v(U∪{j}) for all U⊆N\{i,j} gives the same equalities for v_and and v_or. The full interaction-difference chains are
\[
\begin{aligned}
I_{and}(T\cup\{i\})-I_{and}(T\cup\{j\})
&=\sum_{L\subseteq T\cup\{i\}}(-1)^{|T\cup\{i\}|-|L|}v_{and}(L)-\sum_{L\subseteq T\cup\{j\}}(-1)^{|T\cup\{j\}|-|L|}v_{and}(L)\\
&=\left[\sum_{L\subseteq T}(-1)^{|T\cup\{i\}|-|L|}v_{and}(L)+\sum_{L\subseteq T}(-1)^{|T\cup\{i\}|-|L\cup\{i\}|}v_{and}(L\cup\{i\})\right]\\
&\quad-\left[\sum_{L\subseteq T}(-1)^{|T\cup\{j\}|-|L|}v_{and}(L)+\sum_{L\subseteq T}(-1)^{|T\cup\{j\}|-|L\cup\{j\}|}v_{and}(L\cup\{j\})\right]\\
&=\sum_{L\subseteq T}(-1)^{|T|-|L|}[v_{and}(L\cup\{i\})-v_{and}(L\cup\{j\})]=0,\\
I_{or}(T\cup\{i\})-I_{or}(T\cup\{j\})
&=-\sum_{L\subseteq T\cup\{i\}}(-1)^{|T\cup\{i\}|-|L|}v_{or}(N\setminus L)+\sum_{L\subseteq T\cup\{j\}}(-1)^{|T\cup\{j\}|-|L|}v_{or}(N\setminus L)\\
&=\left[\sum_{L\subseteq T}(-1)^{|T\cup\{j\}|-|L|}v_{or}(N\setminus L)+\sum_{L\subseteq T}(-1)^{|T\cup\{j\}|-|L\cup\{j\}|}v_{or}(N\setminus(L\cup\{j\}))\right]\\
&\quad-\left[\sum_{L\subseteq T}(-1)^{|T\cup\{i\}|-|L|}v_{or}(N\setminus L)+\sum_{L\subseteq T}(-1)^{|T\cup\{i\}|-|L\cup\{i\}|}v_{or}(N\setminus(L\cup\{i\}))\right]\\
&=\sum_{L\subseteq T}(-1)^{|T|-|L|}[v_{or}((N\setminus(L\cup\{i,j\}))\cup\{i\})-v_{or}((N\setminus(L\cup\{i,j\}))\cup\{j\})]=0.
\end{aligned}
\]
Let J(T)=I_and(T)+I_or(T). The complete attribution-difference chain is
\[
\begin{aligned}
\phi(S\cup\{i\})-\phi(S\cup\{j\})
&=\sum_{T\supseteq S\cup\{i\}}\frac{|S\cup\{i\}|}{|T|}J(T)-\sum_{T\supseteq S\cup\{j\}}\frac{|S\cup\{j\}|}{|T|}J(T)\\
&=\left[\sum_{T\supseteq S\cup\{i,j\}}\frac{|S|+1}{|T|}J(T)+\sum_{T\supseteq S\cup\{i\},j\notin T}\frac{|S|+1}{|T|}J(T)\right]\\
&\quad-\left[\sum_{T\supseteq S\cup\{i,j\}}\frac{|S|+1}{|T|}J(T)+\sum_{T\supseteq S\cup\{j\},i\notin T}\frac{|S|+1}{|T|}J(T)\right]\\
&=\sum_{T\supseteq S\cup\{i\},j\notin T}\frac{|S|+1}{|T|}J(T)-\sum_{T\supseteq S\cup\{j\},i\notin T}\frac{|S|+1}{|T|}J(T)\\
&=\sum_{\substack{T\supseteq S\\T\subseteq N\setminus\{i,j\}}}\frac{|S|+1}{|T\cup\{i\}|}J(T\cup\{i\})-\sum_{\substack{T\supseteq S\\T\subseteq N\setminus\{i,j\}}}\frac{|S|+1}{|T\cup\{j\}|}J(T\cup\{j\})\\
&=\sum_{\substack{T\supseteq S\\T\subseteq N\setminus\{i,j\}}}\frac{|S|+1}{|T|+1}\left[(I_{and}(T\cup\{i\})-I_{and}(T\cup\{j\}))+(I_{or}(T\cup\{i\})-I_{or}(T\cup\{j\}))\right]=0.
\end{aligned}
\]
The source concludes φ(S∪{i})=φ(S∪{j}).

# Appendix G.3. Proof of Symmetry β

Source: official PDF pages 19–20. This transcription deliberately preserves the printed ∈ indexing of subsets, the |L| in several OR exponents, the unproved disjointness reduction, and the all-equal-cardinality pairing. They are not repaired in this field.

The source begins: “Without loss of generality, we assume S∩T=∅.” For every K⊇L, K⊆N\(S∪T), T′⊆T with T′≠T, S′⊆S with S′≠S and |S′|=|T′|, put X=K∪S∪T′ and Y=K∪S′∪T. The four printed definitions are
\[
I_{and}(X)=\sum_{J\subseteq X}(-1)^{|X|-|J|}v_{and}(J),\quad
I_{or}(X)=-\sum_{J\subseteq X}(-1)^{|X|-|L|}v_{or}(N\setminus J),
\]
\[
I_{and}(Y)=\sum_{J\subseteq Y}(-1)^{|Y|-|J|}v_{and}(J),\quad
I_{or}(Y)=-\sum_{J\subseteq Y}(-1)^{|Y|-|L|}v_{or}(N\setminus J).
\]
The complete AND-difference calculation is
\[
\begin{aligned}
I_{and}(X)-I_{and}(Y)
&=\sum_{J\subseteq X}(-1)^{|X|-|J|}v_{and}(J)-\sum_{J\subseteq Y}(-1)^{|Y|-|J|}v_{and}(J)\\
&=\sum_{J\subseteq K\cup S'\cup T'}\left[
\sum_{\substack{A\in S\setminus S'\\A\ne S\setminus S'}}(-1)^{|X|-|J\cup A|}v_{and}(J\cup A)
-\sum_{\substack{B\in T\setminus T'\\B\ne T\setminus T'}}(-1)^{|Y|-|J\cup B|}v_{and}(J\cup B)\right]\\
&=\sum_{J\subseteq K\cup S'\cup T'}\sum_{\substack{A\in S\setminus S',\ A\ne S\setminus S'\\ B\in T\setminus T',\ B\ne T\setminus T'\\|A|=|B|}}
(-1)^{|Y|-|J\cup B|}[v_{and}(J\cup A)-v_{and}(J\cup B)]\\
&=0.
\end{aligned}
\]
The complete OR-difference calculation is
\[
\begin{aligned}
I_{or}(X)-I_{or}(Y)
&=-\sum_{J\subseteq X}(-1)^{|X|-|L|}v_{or}(N\setminus J)+\sum_{J\subseteq Y}(-1)^{|Y|-|L|}v_{or}(N\setminus J)\\
&=\sum_{J\subseteq K\cup S'\cup T'}\left[
\sum_{\substack{B\in T\setminus T'\\B\ne T\setminus T'}}(-1)^{|Y|-|J\cup B|}v_{or}(N\setminus(J\cup B))
-\sum_{\substack{A\in S\setminus S'\\A\ne S\setminus S'}}(-1)^{|X|-|J\cup A|}v_{or}(N\setminus(J\cup A))\right]\\
&=\sum_{J\subseteq K\cup S'\cup T'}\sum_{\substack{A\in S\setminus S',\ A\ne S\setminus S'\\B\in T\setminus T',\ B\ne T\setminus T'\\|A|=|B|}}
(-1)^{|Y|-|J\cup B|}[v_{or}(N\setminus(J\cup B))-v_{or}(N\setminus(J\cup A))]\\
&=\sum_{J\subseteq K\cup S'\cup T'}\sum_{\substack{A\in S\setminus S',\ A\ne S\setminus S'\\B\in T\setminus T',\ B\ne T\setminus T'\\|A|=|B|}}
(-1)^{|Y|-|J\cup B|}[v_{or}((N\setminus(J\cup A\cup B))\cup A)-v_{or}((N\setminus(J\cup A\cup B))\cup B)]\\
&=\sum_{J\subseteq K\cup S'\cup T'}\sum_{\substack{A\in S\setminus S',\ A\ne S\setminus S'\\B\in T\setminus T',\ B\ne T\setminus T'\\|A|=|B|}}0=0.
\end{aligned}
\]
Now J_effect(U)=I_and(U)+I_or(U) is a distinct shorthand for the repeated source bracket, not the earlier subset variable J. Eq. (6) gives φ(L∪S) and φ(L∪T). The page-20 chain is
\[
\begin{aligned}
\phi(L\cup S)-\phi(L\cup T)
&=\sum_{K\supseteq L\cup S}\frac{|L\cup S|}{|K|}J_{effect}(K)-\sum_{K\supseteq L\cup T}\frac{|L\cup T|}{|K|}J_{effect}(K)\\
&=\left[\sum_{K\supseteq L\cup S\cup T}\frac{|L\cup S|}{|K|}J_{effect}(K)+\sum_{K\supseteq L\cup S,K\not\supseteq T}\frac{|L\cup S|}{|K|}J_{effect}(K)\right]\\
&\quad-\left[\sum_{K\supseteq L\cup S\cup T}\frac{|L\cup T|}{|K|}J_{effect}(K)+\sum_{K\supseteq L\cup T,K\not\supseteq S}\frac{|L\cup T|}{|K|}J_{effect}(K)\right]\\
&=\sum_{K\supseteq L\cup S,K\not\supseteq T}\frac{|L\cup S|}{|K|}J_{effect}(K)-\sum_{K\supseteq L\cup T,K\not\supseteq S}\frac{|L\cup T|}{|K|}J_{effect}(K)\\
&=\sum_{\substack{K\supseteq L\\K\subseteq N\setminus(S\cup T)}}\sum_{T'\subseteq T,T'\ne T}\frac{|L\cup S|}{|K\cup S\cup T'|}J_{effect}(K\cup S\cup T')\\
&\quad-\sum_{\substack{K\supseteq L\\K\subseteq N\setminus(S\cup T)}}\sum_{S'\subseteq S,S'\ne S}\frac{|L\cup T|}{|K\cup S'\cup T|}J_{effect}(K\cup S'\cup T)\\
&=\sum_{\substack{K\supseteq L\\K\subseteq N\setminus(S\cup T)}}\sum_{\substack{T'\subseteq T,T'\ne T\\S'\subseteq S,S'\ne S\\|S'|=|T'|}}\frac{|L\cup T|}{|K\cup S'\cup T|}
\left[I_{and}(K\cup S\cup T')-I_{and}(K\cup S'\cup T)+I_{or}(K\cup S\cup T')-I_{or}(K\cup S'\cup T)\right]\\
&=0.
\end{aligned}
\]
The source concludes the symmetry-β axiom. The change from separate sums to an all-pairs sum is preserved as printed, even though it is not a bijective reindexing.

# Appendix G.3. Proof of Symmetry β

Source: official PDF pages 19–20. This transcription deliberately preserves the printed ∈ indexing of subsets, the |L| in several OR exponents, the unproved disjointness reduction, and the all-equal-cardinality pairing. They are not repaired in this field.

The source begins: “Without loss of generality, we assume S∩T=∅.” For every K⊇L, K⊆N\(S∪T), T′⊆T with T′≠T, S′⊆S with S′≠S and |S′|=|T′|, put X=K∪S∪T′ and Y=K∪S′∪T. The four printed definitions are
\[
I_{and}(X)=\sum_{J\subseteq X}(-1)^{|X|-|J|}v_{and}(J),\quad
I_{or}(X)=-\sum_{J\subseteq X}(-1)^{|X|-|L|}v_{or}(N\setminus J),
\]
\[
I_{and}(Y)=\sum_{J\subseteq Y}(-1)^{|Y|-|J|}v_{and}(J),\quad
I_{or}(Y)=-\sum_{J\subseteq Y}(-1)^{|Y|-|L|}v_{or}(N\setminus J).
\]
The complete AND-difference calculation is
\[
\begin{aligned}
I_{and}(X)-I_{and}(Y)
&=\sum_{J\subseteq X}(-1)^{|X|-|J|}v_{and}(J)-\sum_{J\subseteq Y}(-1)^{|Y|-|J|}v_{and}(J)\\
&=\sum_{J\subseteq K\cup S'\cup T'}\left[
\sum_{\substack{A\in S\setminus S'\\A\ne S\setminus S'}}(-1)^{|X|-|J\cup A|}v_{and}(J\cup A)
-\sum_{\substack{B\in T\setminus T'\\B\ne T\setminus T'}}(-1)^{|Y|-|J\cup B|}v_{and}(J\cup B)\right]\\
&=\sum_{J\subseteq K\cup S'\cup T'}\sum_{\substack{A\in S\setminus S',\ A\ne S\setminus S'\\ B\in T\setminus T',\ B\ne T\setminus T'\\|A|=|B|}}
(-1)^{|Y|-|J\cup B|}[v_{and}(J\cup A)-v_{and}(J\cup B)]\\
&=0.
\end{aligned}
\]
The complete OR-difference calculation is
\[
\begin{aligned}
I_{or}(X)-I_{or}(Y)
&=-\sum_{J\subseteq X}(-1)^{|X|-|L|}v_{or}(N\setminus J)+\sum_{J\subseteq Y}(-1)^{|Y|-|L|}v_{or}(N\setminus J)\\
&=\sum_{J\subseteq K\cup S'\cup T'}\left[
\sum_{\substack{B\in T\setminus T'\\B\ne T\setminus T'}}(-1)^{|Y|-|J\cup B|}v_{or}(N\setminus(J\cup B))
-\sum_{\substack{A\in S\setminus S'\\A\ne S\setminus S'}}(-1)^{|X|-|J\cup A|}v_{or}(N\setminus(J\cup A))\right]\\
&=\sum_{J\subseteq K\cup S'\cup T'}\sum_{\substack{A\in S\setminus S',\ A\ne S\setminus S'\\B\in T\setminus T',\ B\ne T\setminus T'\\|A|=|B|}}
(-1)^{|Y|-|J\cup B|}[v_{or}(N\setminus(J\cup B))-v_{or}(N\setminus(J\cup A))]\\
&=\sum_{J\subseteq K\cup S'\cup T'}\sum_{\substack{A\in S\setminus S',\ A\ne S\setminus S'\\B\in T\setminus T',\ B\ne T\setminus T'\\|A|=|B|}}
(-1)^{|Y|-|J\cup B|}[v_{or}((N\setminus(J\cup A\cup B))\cup A)-v_{or}((N\setminus(J\cup A\cup B))\cup B)]\\
&=\sum_{J\subseteq K\cup S'\cup T'}\sum_{\substack{A\in S\setminus S',\ A\ne S\setminus S'\\B\in T\setminus T',\ B\ne T\setminus T'\\|A|=|B|}}0=0.
\end{aligned}
\]
Now J_effect(U)=I_and(U)+I_or(U) is a distinct shorthand for the repeated source bracket, not the earlier subset variable J. Eq. (6) gives φ(L∪S) and φ(L∪T). The page-20 chain is
\[
\begin{aligned}
\phi(L\cup S)-\phi(L\cup T)
&=\sum_{K\supseteq L\cup S}\frac{|L\cup S|}{|K|}J_{effect}(K)-\sum_{K\supseteq L\cup T}\frac{|L\cup T|}{|K|}J_{effect}(K)\\
&=\left[\sum_{K\supseteq L\cup S\cup T}\frac{|L\cup S|}{|K|}J_{effect}(K)+\sum_{K\supseteq L\cup S,K\not\supseteq T}\frac{|L\cup S|}{|K|}J_{effect}(K)\right]\\
&\quad-\left[\sum_{K\supseteq L\cup S\cup T}\frac{|L\cup T|}{|K|}J_{effect}(K)+\sum_{K\supseteq L\cup T,K\not\supseteq S}\frac{|L\cup T|}{|K|}J_{effect}(K)\right]\\
&=\sum_{K\supseteq L\cup S,K\not\supseteq T}\frac{|L\cup S|}{|K|}J_{effect}(K)-\sum_{K\supseteq L\cup T,K\not\supseteq S}\frac{|L\cup T|}{|K|}J_{effect}(K)\\
&=\sum_{\substack{K\supseteq L\\K\subseteq N\setminus(S\cup T)}}\sum_{T'\subseteq T,T'\ne T}\frac{|L\cup S|}{|K\cup S\cup T'|}J_{effect}(K\cup S\cup T')\\
&\quad-\sum_{\substack{K\supseteq L\\K\subseteq N\setminus(S\cup T)}}\sum_{S'\subseteq S,S'\ne S}\frac{|L\cup T|}{|K\cup S'\cup T|}J_{effect}(K\cup S'\cup T)\\
&=\sum_{\substack{K\supseteq L\\K\subseteq N\setminus(S\cup T)}}\sum_{\substack{T'\subseteq T,T'\ne T\\S'\subseteq S,S'\ne S\\|S'|=|T'|}}\frac{|L\cup T|}{|K\cup S'\cup T|}
\left[I_{and}(K\cup S\cup T')-I_{and}(K\cup S'\cup T)+I_{or}(K\cup S\cup T')-I_{or}(K\cup S'\cup T)\right]\\
&=0.
\end{aligned}
\]
The source concludes the symmetry-β axiom. The change from separate sums to an all-pairs sum is preserved as printed, even though it is not a bijective reindexing.

# Appendix G.4. Proof of Additivity

Source: official PDF page 20. The original unsupported inference is retained.

For k absent,1,2, the source separately lists the six definitions
\[
\begin{aligned}
I_{and,v}(T)&=\sum_{L\subseteq T}(-1)^{|T|-|L|}v_{and}(L),& I_{or,v}(T)&=-\sum_{L\subseteq T}(-1)^{|T|-|L|}v_{or}(N\setminus L),\\
I_{and,v_1}(T)&=\sum_{L\subseteq T}(-1)^{|T|-|L|}v_{and,1}(L),& I_{or,v_1}(T)&=-\sum_{L\subseteq T}(-1)^{|T|-|L|}v_{or,1}(N\setminus L),\\
I_{and,v_2}(T)&=\sum_{L\subseteq T}(-1)^{|T|-|L|}v_{and,2}(L),& I_{or,v_2}(T)&=-\sum_{L\subseteq T}(-1)^{|T|-|L|}v_{or,2}(N\setminus L).
\end{aligned}
\]
Here v=v_and+v_or, v₁=v_and,1+v_or,1 and v₂=v_and,2+v_or,2. It claims from v=v₁+v₂ that I_and,v=I_and,v₁+I_and,v₂ and I_or,v=I_or,v₁+I_or,v₂. It then lists Eq. (6) for each of the three games and calculates
\[
\begin{aligned}
\phi_v(S)
&=\sum_{T\supseteq S}\frac{|S|}{|T|}[I_{and,v}(T)+I_{or,v}(T)]\\
&=\sum_{T\supseteq S}\frac{|S|}{|T|}[(I_{and,v_1}(T)+I_{and,v_2}(T))+(I_{or,v_1}(T)+I_{or,v_2}(T))]\\

\end{aligned}
\]

proof_steps.title: 按排列位置证明逆阶数权重
proof_steps.body_md: 令 $R=N\setminus\{i\}$、$L\subseteq R$、$l=|L|$、$n=|R|+1$，$w(U)=|U|!(n-|U|-1)!/n!$。均匀随机排列中 $w(U)$ 是 $U$ 恰为 $i$ 前驱集的概率；$L$ 全在 $i$ 前当且仅当 $i$ 在 $L\cup\{i\}$ 中最后出现，概率为 $1/(l+1)$。按 $|U|=l+k$ 分组，满足 $L\subseteq U\subseteq R$ 的集合数为 $\binom{n-1-l}{k}$，且 $w(U)=1/[n\binom{n-1}{l+k}]$，所以得到原显示二项式系数等式。OR 不交背景用补集双射或最先出现计数得到同一值。Lean 核验等价阶乘前驱有限和；按基数分组到显示二项式式子的解释是人类适配，未另作直接数值索引声明。

en.overview: Complete the coefficient identity used without expansion in the author proof.

proof_steps.title: Prove reciprocal-order weights by permutation positions
proof_steps.body_md: Let $R=N\setminus\{i\}$, $L\subseteq R$, $l=|L|$, $n=|R|+1$, and $w(U)=|U|!(n-|U|-1)!/n!$. In a uniform random permutation, $w(U)$ is the probability that $U$ is exactly the predecessor set of $i$. All of $L$ precedes $i$ precisely when $i$ is last in $L\cup\{i\}$, with probability $1/(l+1)$. Grouping by $|U|=l+k$ yields $\binom{n-1-l}{k}$ containing backgrounds, each with $w(U)=1/[n\binom{n-1}{l+k}]$, proving the displayed binomial identity. A complement bijection or first-position count gives the same OR value. Lean checks the equivalent factorial predecessor sum; grouping it into the displayed cardinality-indexed formula is the human adaptation, without a separate numeric-index declaration.

en.title: Signed superset binomial weight
en.overview: Write a superset U as L union a subset of its complement.
assumptions: $R$ is finite and $L\subseteq R$, including $L=\varnothing$ and $L=R$.

proof_steps.title: Use a complement bijection and the binomial expansion
proof_steps.body_md: Write uniquely $U=L\cup W$ with $W\subseteq R\setminus L$, so $|U|=|L|+|W|$. The finite sum becomes $(-1/2)^{|L|}\sum_{W\subseteq R\setminus L}(-1/2)^{|W|}$. There are $\binom{|R|-|L|}{j}$ subsets of size $j$; the binomial theorem gives inner sum $(1-1/2)^{|R|-|L|}$. Multiplication yields $(-1)^{|L|}/2^{|R|}$, including $R=L$, where the inner sum is the single empty term $1$.

en.title: Eq. (10): exact AND/OR reconstruction
en.overview: Apply Möbius and complement reconstruction separately, retaining the sum of the component baselines.
assumptions: $N$ is finite. Fix the same input, model, and input baseline. The raw output baseline need not be zero.

definitions.body_md: Fix a finite universe $N$, input $x$, and input baseline vector $r$; put $g(U)=v(x_U)$ and $b=g(\varnothing)$. Local $a=g_{and}$ and $o=g_{or}$ abbreviate the two source components, $a(U)=g(U)/2+\gamma_U$ and $o(U)=g(U)/2-\gamma_U$. Local $A=I_{g_{and}}$ and $O=O_{g_{or}}$ abbreviate the AND component’s Möbius dividend and the nonempty OR negative complementary dividend; $J=A+O$. The raw output baseline need not vanish.

proof_steps.title: Invert the AND and OR components
proof_steps.body_md: Möbius inversion gives a(S)=a(empty)+∑_{nonempty T⊆S}A(T). Apply the same inversion to h(L)=-o(N\L); its nonempty coefficients are O(T). Intersecting subsets are all subsets of N except those of $N\setminus S$, so their sum is h(N)-h($N\setminus S$)=o(S)-o(empty). Add the component baselines to obtain b and the claimed identity. At S=empty both activated sums vanish, so matching remains exact.

en.title: Exact AND effects of binary monomials
en.overview: Under the displayed binary zero-baseline masking game, each monomial is a pure AND game.
assumptions: $N$ is finite. Fix the same input, model, and input baseline. The raw output baseline need not be zero.

definitions.body_md: Use binary inputs and zero input baseline, with masked game $g(U)=f(x_U)$ and source monomial supports $T_k$. This entry computes the total game’s Harsanyi AND dividend $I_g$, distinct from the learned split’s $A,O$.

proof_steps.title: Identify AND supports of binary monomials
proof_steps.body_md: For binary inputs and zero input baseline, $\prod_{j\in T_k}(x_U)_j=\mathbf1_{T_k\subseteq U}\prod_{j\in T_k}x_j$. Thus $g$ is a finite sum of pure AND games with weights $w_k\prod_{j\in T_k}x_j$. A pure AND dividend is its weight at support $T_k$ and zero elsewhere; interaction linearity gives the displayed formula. Distinct source supports require no duplicate merging. At the all-one input the product is $1$; zero coordinates remove the corresponding monomial. This is the total game’s Harsanyi support, without claiming uniqueness or the same supports for learned $A,O$, and without treating approximate network fitting as an exact identity of the target function.

shared_proofs.title: 公共证明：所有交互精确重构每一个掩码输出

assumptions.text_md: S 是有限变量集合。g 与 d 是定义在有限变量子集上的任意实值函数；不要求连续、可微、独立性或零输出基线。
U 表示变量总体，\(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{fin}}(U)\) 表示其所有有限子集。每次参与求和的 S、T 都有限；变量总体本身可以无限。论文应用则固定有限总体 N，只讨论 \(2^N\)。

definitions.text_md: 交互是有限交替和。\(T\subseteq S\) 保证 |T|≤|S|，因此指数 \(|S|-|T|\) 是非负整数。
\(R_d\) 是在给定保留变量集 S 上累加所有被激活的系数。
插入差分比较保留 i 与掩码 i 两种状态。下面的插入引理只在 \(i\notin S\) 时使用。

shared_proofs.overview: 每次插入新变量 $i$，把子集分成含 $i$ 与不含 $i$ 两类。含 $i$ 的交互等于插入差分的交互；对两类分别应用加强归纳假设，中间输出相消，留下当前输出。

proof_steps.title: 辅助引理：为什么子集能分成两组
proof_steps.body_md: 固定有限集合 S 及不属于 S 的变量 i。\(S\cup \{i\}\) 的任何子集 A，要么不含 i，这时 A 本身就是 S 的子集；要么含 i，这时唯一地写成 \(A=T\cup \{i\}\)，其中 \(T=A\setminus \{i\}\subseteq S\)。两类互不重叠，且各自覆盖所有可能情况，所以对任意实值函数 F 可以把有限和改写为下面的两组和。没有遗漏空集：它出现在第一组 \(T=\varnothing\)；第二组 \(T=\varnothing\) 对应 {i}。
proof_steps.justification: 子集与不含/含 i 两类的显式一一对应。

lean_refs.explanation_md: 插入引理证明内实际使用子集拆分；这一步没有另增一个项目定理。

proof_steps.title: 辅助引理：展开符号，得到插入差分
proof_steps.body_md: 把上一步用于交互 \(I_g(S\cup \{i\})\) 的定义。每个 \(T\subseteq S\) 都满足 \(i\notin T\)，因此 \(|S\cup \{i\}|=|S|+1\)、\(|T\cup \{i\}|=|T|+1\)。令 \(k=|S|-|T|\ge 0\)：第一组的系数是 \((-1)^{k+1}=-(-1)^k\)；第二组的系数是 \((-1)^k\)。把同一 T 的两项合并，得到 \((-1)^k\)[\(g(T\cup \{i\})−g(T)\)]。最后一行正是 \(I_{\Delta_i g}(S)\) 的定义。
proof_steps.justification: \(i\notin S\) 及 \(T\subseteq S\) 给出两个插入基数；整数幂的递推关系给出负号；有限和逐项相加。

lean_refs.explanation_md: 这个三行等式是已存在 interaction_insert 的完整数学内容；h1/h2 位于该声明证明内。

proof_steps.title: 主证明：加强归纳命题，并处理空集
proof_steps.body_md:
对有限集合 S 作插入归纳，但归纳命题必须说“对任意集合函数 g 都有 \(R_{I_g}(S)=g(S)\)”。不能只固定最初的 g 后归纳，因为插入一步还要对新函数 \(\Delta_i g\) 使用归纳假设。

当 \(S=\varnothing\) 时，空集只有一个子集，即自身。定义中的指数是 0，(−1)^0=1，所以 \(I_g(\varnothing )=g(\varnothing )\)，而重构和也只有这一项。这是归纳起点；无需且不能在这里默默令 \(g(\varnothing )\)=0。
proof_steps.justification: 有限集合插入归纳；空集的子集族只有空集本身；空集交互公式。

lean_refs.explanation_md: 归纳语句 generalizing v 以及 empty 分支都在 reconstruction 的现有证明内。

proof_steps.title: 主证明：对两组和分别使用归纳假设
proof_steps.body_md: 现在设 \(i\notin S\)，并假设任意函数 h 在 S 上都满足 \(R_{I_h}(S)\)=h(S)。第一步的拆分把 \(S\cup \{i\}\) 上的重构和写成两组。对第二组中的每个 \(T\subseteq S\)，仍有 \(i\notin T\)，所以第二步的插入交互引理可以逐项使用。得到的第二组是 \(\Delta_i g\) 在 S 上的交互总和。对第一组用归纳假设 h=g，对第二组用归纳假设 h=\(\Delta_i g\)，便分别得到 \(g(S)\) 与 \(\Delta_i g(S)\)。这里明确使用了两次同一个归纳假设，而不是假设差分的结论未经证明成立。
proof_steps.justification: 子集拆分；插入交互引理逐项使用；加强归纳假设适用于任意集合函数。

lean_refs.explanation_md: 现有代码的 sum_congr、ih v 和 ih (marginal v i) 分别实现逐项替换和两次归纳应用。

proof_steps.title: 主证明：消去中间输出，完成归纳
proof_steps.body_md: 按插入差分的定义，\(\Delta_i g(S)=g(S\cup \{i\})-g(S)\)。将其代入上一步，\(g(S)\) 与 −\(g(S)\) 在实数加法中消去，得到所需的 \(g(S\cup \{i\})\)。空集起点与每次插入的步骤已经覆盖所有有限 S，因此对任意有限 S 的重构恒等式成立。论文中只需把这里的 \(g(S)\) 换成固定模型和掩码规则给出的 \(v(x_S)\)。
proof_steps.justification: 插入差分定义与实数加减法；有限集合归纳结论。

lean.adapter_code:
theorem interaction_insert (v : Game α) (S : Finset α) (i : α) (hi : i ∉ S) :
    interaction v (insert i S) = interaction (marginal v i) S := by
  unfold interaction marginal
  rw [sum_powerset_insert hi]
  have h1 : ∀ T ∈ S.powerset,
      (-1 : ℝ) ^ ((insert i S).card - T.card) * v T =
      -((-1 : ℝ) ^ (S.card - T.card) * v T) := by
    intro T hT
    have hTS := card_le_card (mem_powerset.mp hT)
    rw [card_insert_of_notMem hi]
    have he : S.card + 1 - T.card = (S.card - T.card) + 1 := by omega
    rw [he, pow_succ]
    ring
  have h2 : ∀ T ∈ S.powerset,
      (-1 : ℝ) ^ ((insert i S).card - (insert i T).card) * v (insert i T) =
      (-1 : ℝ) ^ (S.card - T.card) * v (insert i T) := by
    intro T hT
    have hiT : i ∉ T := fun hit => hi ((mem_powerset.mp hT) hit)
    rw [card_insert_of_notMem hi, card_insert_of_notMem hiT]
    simp
  rw [sum_congr rfl h1, sum_congr rfl h2, ← sum_add_distrib]
  apply sum_congr rfl
  intro T _
  ring

/-- All dividends reconstruct every finite coalition, without a baseline assumption. -/

theorem reconstruction (v : Game α) (S : Finset α) :
    reconstruct (interaction v) S = v S := by
  induction S using Finset.induction_on generalizing v with
  | empty => simp
  | @insert i S hi ih =>
    unfold reconstruct
    rw [sum_powerset_insert hi]
    have h : ∀ T ∈ S.powerset,
        interaction v (insert i T) = interaction (marginal v i) T := by
      intro T hT
      exact interaction_insert v T i (fun hit => hi ((mem_powerset.mp hT) hit))
    rw [sum_congr rfl h]
    change reconstruct (interaction v) S + reconstruct (interaction (marginal v i)) S = _
    rw [ih v, ih (marginal v i)]
    simp [marginal]

/-- The converse Boolean Möbius inversion: transforming subset sums recovers coefficients. -/

en.title: Shared proof: exact reconstruction of every masked output

assumptions.text_md: The coalition is finite. The games and coefficient functions are arbitrary real-valued functions on finite subsets; continuity, differentiability, independence and a zero output baseline are unnecessary.
The ambient universe may be infinite, but every coalition in a sum is finite. Paper applications fix a finite universe and use its powerset.

definitions.text_md: The interaction is a finite alternating sum. Since the summation subset is contained in the target, the cardinality difference in its exponent is a nonnegative integer.
Reconstruction sums all coefficients activated by the retained-variable set.
The insertion difference compares retaining the distinguished variable with masking it. The insertion lemma below is used only when that variable is absent from the target.

en.overview: Insertion separates subsets with and without the new variable. The insertion interaction becomes a finite difference; strengthened induction reconstructs both games and cancels the intermediate output.
en.completion_scope: The public finite-set reconstruction theorem and its actual library induction; paper specializations are separate.
en.example_md: For two variables with mask outputs 2, 5, 7 and 13, the dividends are 2, 3, 5 and 3. Their full sum is 13, the empty-mask sum is 2, and singleton reconstruction gives 5 and 7. If only the full output 13 were required, coefficients 0, 0, 0 and 13 would also fit that one mask but fail all others. Hence the universal mask requirement matters.
caveats: The human proof explains the existing library declarations; its five steps do not introduce five new Lean theorems. The checked scope consists of the library theorem and separately compiled paper adapters.
Every subset sum includes the empty coefficient. If it is omitted, add the output baseline outside the sum.

The source uses double sums and binomial cancellation; the library uses insertion induction or converse inversion. These are separately identified proof routes, not a claim of line-by-line formal translation.

proof_steps.title: Partition the subsets into two families
proof_steps.body_md: Fix finite $S$ and $i\notin S$. Every subset of $S\cup\{i\}$ either excludes $i$, and is a subset $T$ of $S$, or includes $i$, and uniquely equals $T\cup\{i\}$ with $T\subseteq S$. The families are disjoint and exhaustive, so any finite sum of a function $F$ splits into these two sums. The empty subset occurs in the first family; empty $T$ in the second family produces $\{i\}$.
proof_steps.justification: The explicit bijections for subsets with and without the inserted variable.

proof_steps.title: Expand the signs to obtain the insertion difference
proof_steps.body_md: Every $T\subseteq S$ excludes $i$, so the two inserted cardinalities are $|S|+1$ and $|T|+1$. Put $k=|S|-|T|\ge0$. The coefficient of $g(T)$ is $(-1)^{k+1}=-(-1)^k$, and the coefficient of $g(T\cup\{i\})$ is $(-1)^k$. Combining the paired terms gives $(-1)^k[g(T\cup\{i\})-g(T)]$. The resulting sum is the interaction of $\Delta_i g$ on $S$.
proof_steps.justification: Insertion cardinalities, the recurrence for integer powers, and finite distributivity.

proof_steps.title: Strengthen the induction statement and handle the empty set
proof_steps.body_md: Induct by inserting elements into finite $S$, with the strengthened statement that reconstruction holds for every game $g$. This quantification is necessary because the next step applies induction to the new game $\Delta_i g$. When $S=\varnothing$, its only subset is itself; the exponent is zero, so both interaction and reconstruction equal $g(\varnothing)$. No zero-baseline assumption is used.
proof_steps.justification: Finite-set insertion induction and the exact empty-interaction formula.

proof_steps.title: Apply induction to each of the two sums
proof_steps.body_md: Assume that every game $h$ is reconstructed on $S$, and let $i\notin S$. Split the reconstruction on $S\cup\{i\}$ into the two families from the first step. In the family containing $i$, each $T\subseteq S$ still excludes $i$, so apply the insertion-difference identity term by term. The two sums become reconstruction for $g$ and reconstruction for $\Delta_i g$ on $S$. The same strengthened induction hypothesis gives $g(S)$ and $\Delta_i g(S)$ respectively.
proof_steps.justification: Subset partition, the insertion identity, and induction quantified over all games.

proof_steps.title: Cancel the intermediate output and finish induction
proof_steps.body_md: By definition, $\Delta_i g(S)=g(S\cup\{i\})-g(S)$. Adding it to $g(S)$ cancels the intermediate value and leaves the required output on the inserted set. The empty case and insertion step cover every finite set. For a paper application, instantiate the game with $g(S)=v(x_S)$ using one fixed model, input and mask rule.
proof_steps.justification: The finite-difference definition and real addition and subtraction.

shared_proofs.title: 公共证明：同时重构所有掩码输出的系数唯一

assumptions.text_md: S 是有限变量集合。g 与 d 是定义在有限变量子集上的任意实值函数；不要求连续、可微、独立性或零输出基线。
U 表示变量总体，\(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{fin}}(U)\) 表示其所有有限子集。每次参与求和的 S、T 都有限；变量总体本身可以无限。论文应用则固定有限总体 N，只讨论 \(2^N\)。
同一组系数 d 必须重构定义域内每一个有限子集的输出，包括空集。只在一个指定集合上重构不够。

definitions.text_md: 交互是有限交替和。\(T\subseteq S\) 保证 |T|≤|S|，因此指数 \(|S|-|T|\) 是非负整数。
\(R_d\) 是在给定保留变量集 S 上累加所有被激活的系数。
插入差分比较保留 i 与掩码 i 两种状态。下面的插入引理只在 \(i\notin S\) 时使用。

shared_proofs.overview: 把“对系数求子集和”再做一次交替差分，会恢复原系数。这是逆向 Möbius 反演 \(I_{R_d}=d\)。先证明这个辅助结论，再把“所有掩码上 \(R_d=g\)”的假设代入，就得到 \(d=I_g\)。下面完整证明所需的逆向反演，给出唯一性成立的理由。

proof_steps.title: 辅助引理：逆向反演的归纳起点
proof_steps.body_md:
先暂时不使用 \(R_d=g\)，单独证明任意系数函数 d 都满足 \(I_{R_d}(S)=d(S)\)。同样对有限 S 插入归纳，并把 d 保留为任意函数，因为插入步骤会引入新函数 e。

若 \(S=\varnothing\)，则 \(R_d(\varnothing )=d(\varnothing )\)。再由空集交互等于被变换函数的空集值，得 \(I_{R_d}(\varnothing )=R_d(\varnothing )=d(\varnothing )\)。这是逆向反演的起点，也说明空集系数并非可以随意选择的额外自由参数。
proof_steps.justification: 重构定义、空集交互公式与加强归纳。

lean_refs.explanation_md: interaction_reconstruct 对 S 归纳并 generalizing d；这一步为其 empty 分支。

proof_steps.title: 辅助引理：重构函数的差分也是一个重构
proof_steps.body_md:
设 \(i\notin S\)，并定义新的系数函数 \(e(U)=d(U\cup \{i\})\)。对任意 \(T\subseteq S\)，都有 \(i\notin T\)，可将 \(R_d(T\cup \{i\})\) 按不含/含 i 的子集拆成 \(R_d(T)\) 加 \(\sum _{U\subseteq T}d(U\cup \{i\})\)。减去 \(R_d(T)\) 后，留下的恰好是 \(R_e(T)\)。

注意该等式只在 \(T\subseteq S\) 的范围使用。若 T 已含 i，子集拆分就不再是两类互不重叠；这个局部等式不需要、也不能强行推广到不受 \(T\subseteq S\) 限制的每个 T。
proof_steps.formula_tex: \begin{aligned}(\Delta_i R_d)(T)&=R_d(T\cup\{i\})-R_d(T)\\&=\left(\sum_{U\subseteq T}d(U)+\sum_{U\subseteq T}d(U\cup\{i\})\right)-\sum_{U\subseteq T}d(U)\\&=\sum_{U\subseteq T}e(U)=R_e(T),\qquad T\subseteq S.\end{aligned}
proof_steps.justification: \(i\notin T\)；子集拆分；相同有限和消去；e 与 \(R_e\) 的定义。

lean_refs.explanation_md: 库证明中的局部 h 使用 sum_powerset_insert；e 在代码中是 fun T => d (insert i T)。

proof_steps.title: 辅助引理：从局部一致性完成插入步骤
proof_steps.body_md: 先用重构证明中的插入交互引理，得到 \(I_{R_d}(S\cup \{i\})=I_{\Delta_i R_d}(S)\)。交互 \(I_h(S)\) 只读取 h 在 S 的子集上的值；第二步已经逐个证明 \(\Delta_i R_d(T)=R_e(T)\)，故两种函数在这次交替和中的每一项相同。因此 \(I_{\Delta_i R_d}(S)=I_{R_e}(S)\)。最后用“对任意系数函数”的归纳假设，将 \(I_{R_e}(S)\) 化为 \(e(S)=d(S\cup \{i\})\)。这样证明了逆向反演在插入集合上的结论。
proof_steps.justification: 插入交互引理；交互对参与求和的局部函数值保持一致；加强归纳假设。

lean_refs.explanation_md: 这里只要求在 S 的所有子集上相同，不要求两函数处处相同。
库证明的 rw [h, ih] 完成该辅助引理。

proof_steps.title: 主证明：将全部掩码的重构假设代入
proof_steps.body_md: 现在恢复假设 ∀T，\(R_d(T)=g(T)\)。固定任意 S。由刚证完的逆向反演，\(d(S)=I_{R_d}(S)\)。在定义 \(I_{R_d}(S)\) 的有限和中，每个 U 都满足 \(U\subseteq S\)，重构假设给出 \(R_d(U)=g(U)\)。逐项替换后，该和就是 \(I_g(S)\)。因此 \(d(S)=I_g(S)\)。这一步使用的是同一组 d 在所有掩码上的假设，而不是每个 S 临时选一组系数。
proof_steps.justification: 逆向反演与逐个子集上的重构假设。

lean_refs.explanation_md: reconstruction_unique 中先改写 interaction_reconstruct，再用 interaction_congr 将 h T 代入。

proof_steps.title: 主证明：逐点相等与适用范围
proof_steps.body_md:
S 是任意有限子集，所以 d 与 \(I_g\) 在定义域的每个输入上取相同值，这正是两个函数相等的含义。本公共命题的量词遍历 U 的所有有限子集；应用于论文时把总体固定为有限 N，函数定义域随之取为 \(2^N\)。

特别取 \(S=\varnothing\)，重构假设强制 \(d(\varnothing )=g(\varnothing )\)。取 \(S=\{i\}\)，又强制 \(d(\{i\})=g(\{i\})−g(\varnothing )\)。继续增加集合，新的最高阶系数会被已经确定的低阶子集系数唯一决定；这解释了原论文按阶数归纳的直观路线。
proof_steps.justification: 函数外延性；论文适配使用固定有限总体。

lean_refs.explanation_md: funext S 在声明开头说明函数相等的含义。

shared_proofs.example_md:
取 \(N=\{1,2\}\)，并指定 \(g(\varnothing)=2\)、\(g(\{1\})=5\)、\(g(\{2\})=7\)、\(g(\{1,2\})=13\)。任何满足全部掩码重构的 d 都必须依次满足
\[d(\varnothing)=2,\quad d(\{1\})=5-2=3,\quad d(\{2\})=7-2=5,\]
\[d(\{1,2\})=13-2-3-5=3.\]
如果只要求完整输入输出等于 13，另一组 \(d(\varnothing),d(\{1\}),d(\{2\}),d(\{1,2\})=(0,0,0,13)\) 也能满足这一条等式，却在全掩码时输出 0、在单变量掩码时也输出 0。因此“所有 \(S\subseteq N\)”的量词不可删除。

theorem interaction_reconstruct (d : Game α) (S : Finset α) :
    interaction (reconstruct d) S = d S := by
  induction S using Finset.induction_on generalizing d with
  | empty => simp
  | @insert i S hi ih =>
    rw [interaction_insert _ _ _ hi]
    have h : interaction (marginal (reconstruct d) i) S =
        interaction (reconstruct (fun T => d (insert i T))) S := by
      apply interaction_congr
      intro T hT
      have hiT : i ∉ T := fun hit => hi (hT hit)
      simp only [marginal, reconstruct, sum_powerset_insert hiT, add_sub_cancel_left]
    rw [h, ih]

/-- Dividends are the unique coefficients that reconstruct all coalitions. -/

theorem reconstruction_unique (v d : Game α)
    (h : ∀ S, reconstruct d S = v S) : d = interaction v := by
  funext S
  rw [← interaction_reconstruct d S]
  apply interaction_congr
  intro T _
  exact h T

en.title: Shared proof: uniqueness of coefficients reconstructing all masks

assumptions.text_md: The coalition is finite. The games and coefficient functions are arbitrary real-valued functions on finite subsets; continuity, differentiability, independence and a zero output baseline are unnecessary.
The ambient universe may be infinite, but every coalition in a sum is finite. Paper applications fix a finite universe and use its powerset.
The same coefficients must reconstruct every finite subset in the domain, including the empty set. Reconstruction at one specified coalition is insufficient.

definitions.text_md: The interaction is a finite alternating sum. Since the summation subset is contained in the target, the cardinality difference in its exponent is a nonnegative integer.
Reconstruction sums all coefficients activated by the retained-variable set.
The insertion difference compares retaining the distinguished variable with masking it. The insertion lemma below is used only when that variable is absent from the target.

en.overview: Prove converse Möbius inversion for arbitrary coefficients, then substitute the reconstruction equality at every mask and conclude pointwise equality.
en.completion_scope: Coefficient uniqueness and the converse inversion actually used by the library; finite-universe paper quantifiers are recorded by separate adapters.
en.example_md: For two variables with mask outputs 2, 5, 7 and 13, the dividends are 2, 3, 5 and 3. Their full sum is 13, the empty-mask sum is 2, and singleton reconstruction gives 5 and 7. If only the full output 13 were required, coefficients 0, 0, 0 and 13 would also fit that one mask but fail all others. Hence the universal mask requirement matters.
caveats: Uniqueness concerns coefficients for one fixed game and the same AND activation rule. It does not assert uniqueness of every explanation framework, causal model or AND–OR decomposition.
The source inducts on cardinality; the library proves converse inversion. This text fully explains the route actually used by the library.
Every subset, including the empty one, must be reconstructed exactly. Fitting only the full input, or fitting approximately, does not satisfy the theorem.

proof_steps.title: Prove converse inversion at the empty set
proof_steps.body_md: First prove $I_{R_d}(S)=d(S)$ for an arbitrary coefficient function $d$, without using the reconstruction hypothesis. Induct on finite $S$ and keep $d$ universally quantified. At the empty set, $R_d(\varnothing)=d(\varnothing)$, and the empty interaction of this game has that same value. Thus the empty coefficient is fixed rather than an additional free parameter.
proof_steps.justification: The definitions and strengthened finite-set induction.

proof_steps.title: The difference of a reconstruction is another reconstruction
proof_steps.body_md: For $i\notin S$, define $e(U)=d(U\cup\{i\})$. Every $T\subseteq S$ excludes $i$, so splitting the subsets of $T\cup\{i\}$ gives $R_d(T\cup\{i\})=R_d(T)+\sum_{U\subseteq T}d(U\cup\{i\})$. Subtraction leaves $R_e(T)$. This identity is used only for $T\subseteq S$: when $i\in T$, the two-family argument would no longer be disjoint.
proof_steps.justification: The subset partition, cancellation of finite sums, and the definition of the new coefficient function.

proof_steps.title: Use local equality to prove the insertion step
proof_steps.body_md: The insertion lemma gives $I_{R_d}(S\cup\{i\})=I_{\Delta_i R_d}(S)$. The interaction on $S$ reads only values at subsets of $S$, where the previous step proves that $\Delta_i R_d$ equals $R_e$. Hence its interaction equals $I_{R_e}(S)$. Apply the induction hypothesis for the arbitrary function $e$ to obtain $e(S)=d(S\cup\{i\})$. This proves converse inversion on the inserted set.
proof_steps.justification: Insertion differences, congruence on the subsets actually used, and strengthened induction.

proof_steps.title: Substitute the reconstruction hypothesis for every mask
proof_steps.body_md: Restore the assumption that the same $d$ satisfies $R_d(T)=g(T)$ at every finite $T$. For arbitrary $S$, converse inversion gives $d(S)=I_{R_d}(S)$. In this finite sum every argument $U$ is a subset of $S$, so the assumption replaces $R_d(U)$ by $g(U)$ term by term. The resulting sum is $I_g(S)$. Coefficients are not chosen afresh for each mask.
proof_steps.justification: Converse inversion and the reconstruction equality at each subset.

proof_steps.title: Conclude function equality and check the application domain
proof_steps.body_md: Since $S$ is arbitrary, equality at every finite input gives $d=I_g$. The public result quantifies over all finite subsets of a universe that may itself be infinite; a paper application restricts this universe to its finite $N$. In particular, the empty mask forces $d(\varnothing)=g(\varnothing)$, and a singleton forces $d(\{i\})=g(\{i\})-g(\varnothing)$. Higher coefficients are then fixed by the already determined proper-subset coefficients.
proof_steps.justification: Function extensionality and the finite-universe paper specialization.

definitions.body_md: Fix a finite universe $N$. A game $g:\mathcal P(N)\to\mathbb R$ has output baseline $b=g(\varnothing)$ and interaction $I_g(A)=\sum_{U\subseteq A}(-1)^{|A|-|U|}g(U)$. proof_steps.title: Handle every case in which the target is not contained
proof_steps.body_md: If $T\not\subseteq S$, no subset $U$ of $S$ can contain $T$. Thus every output and summand is zero. This includes both proper-subset and incomparable cases; the original proof omitted the latter.

proof_steps.title: Evaluate at the target itself
proof_steps.body_md: If $S=T$, only the subset $U=T$ contributes the output $c$, with coefficient 1; every proper subset contributes zero. This also covers the empty target, whose only summand is the empty-set output $c$.

proof_steps.title: Cancel on strict supersets
proof_steps.body_md: For $T\subsetneq S$, the potentially nonzero subsets uniquely equal $T\cup B$, with $B\subseteq S\setminus T$. Their exponents are $|S\setminus T|-|B|$. Choose an element of the nonempty difference, and pair each $B$ excluding it with the subset including it. The two signs are opposite, so the whole sum vanishes.

proof_steps.title: Check the empty target and an incomparable set
proof_steps.body_md: An empty target gives the constant game $c$, with only its empty dividend nonzero. With $N=\{1,2\}$, $T=\{1\}$ and $c=3$, the four outputs are 0, 3, 0 and 3, and the dividends are 0, 3, 0 and 0. The incomparable set $\{2\}$ is covered by the first case.

definitions.body_md: Fix a finite universe $N$. A game $g:\mathcal P(N)\to\mathbb R$ has output baseline $b=g(\varnothing)$ and interaction $I_g(A)=\sum_{U\subseteq A}(-1)^{|A|-|U|}g(U)$. shared_proofs.title: 共享辅助证明：包含全部空集边界的有限阶乘恒等式
assumptions: $T,E\subseteq N$，$T\cap E=\varnothing$；$k\in\mathbb N$、$k>0$；$m=|E|$。

definitions.body_md: 固定有限总体 $N$。集合函数 $g:\mathcal P(N)\to\mathbb R$ 的输出基线为 $b=g(\varnothing)$，交互为 $I_g(A)=\sum_{U\subseteq A}(-1)^{|A|-|U|}g(U)$。记 $w_A=I_g(A)$。所有子集和包括空集，且 $w_\varnothing=b$。差分为 $\Delta_Tg(S)=\sum_{L\subseteq T}(-1)^{|T|-|L|}g(L\cup S)$。原始输出不要求零基线；中心化函数 $g_0=g-b$ 仅使空交互变为零。

proof_steps.title: 完整辅助引理：有限阶乘卷积
proof_steps.body_md: 对任意有限集合 $R$、非负整数 $a,b$，记 $m=|R|$，$F_R(a,b)=\sum_{A\subseteq R}(a+|A|)!(b+m-|A|)!$。对 $R$ 作插入归纳，并加强归纳命题为对所有 $a,b$ 成立。$R=\varnothing$ 时两边都是 $a!b!$。插入新变量 $i\notin R$ 后，按 $A$ 是否含 $i$ 分组得到 $F_{R\cup\{i\}}(a,b)=F_R(a,b+1)+F_R(a+1,b)$。归纳假设给出的两项有共同分母 $(a+b+2)!$ 和共同大阶乘 $(a+b+m+2)!$，小阶乘相加为 $a!(b+1)!+(a+1)!b!=a!b!(a+b+2)$。约去正数 $a+b+2$ 得插入后的公式。全部阶乘为正，除法合法；论证包括 $a=0$、$b=0$、$m=0$。

en.title: Shared auxiliary proof: finite factorial convolution, including empty boundaries
assumptions: $T,E\subseteq N$, $T\cap E=\varnothing$; $k\in\mathbb N$, $k>0$; $m=|E|$.

definitions.body_md: Fix a finite universe $N$. A game $g:\mathcal P(N)\to\mathbb R$ has output baseline $b=g(\varnothing)$ and interaction $I_g(A)=\sum_{U\subseteq A}(-1)^{|A|-|U|}g(U)$. Write $w_A=I_g(A)$. Every subset sum includes the empty set, and $w_\varnothing=b$. The finite difference is $\Delta_Tg(S)=\sum_{L\subseteq T}(-1)^{|T|-|L|}g(L\cup S)$. No zero output baseline is assumed. Centering $g_0=g-b$ removes only the empty dividend.

proof_steps.title: Prove the finite factorial convolution
proof_steps.body_md: For finite $R$ of size $m$, define $F_R(a,b)=\sum_{A\subseteq R}(a+|A|)!(b+m-|A|)!$. Induct on $R$ with the statement strengthened to every nonnegative $a,b$. At the empty set both sides are $a!b!$. Inserting a new element splits the sum as $F_R(a,b+1)+F_R(a+1,b)$. The induction expressions share denominator $(a+b+2)!$ and large factorial $(a+b+m+2)!$. The smaller factorials combine as $a!(b+1)!+(a+1)!b!=a!b!(a+b+2)$. Cancelling this positive factor proves the formula on the inserted set. Every factorial denominator is positive; zero values of $a,b,m$ are included.

proof_steps.title: Sum weights over all supersets of a fixed subset
proof_steps.body_md: Let $k>0$, $L\subseteq E$, $m=|E|$, $l=|L|$ and $R=E\setminus L$. Each $S$ with $L\subseteq S\subseteq E$ uniquely equals $L\cup A$ with $A\subseteq R$. Thus $|S|=l+|A|$ and $|R|=m-l$. Apply the preceding convolution with $a=l$ and $b=k-1$. Use $k(k-1)!=k!$ and cancel the positive large factorial $(m+k)!$ to obtain the displayed weight sum. Both $L=\varnothing$ and $L=E$ are included.

proof_steps.title: Exchange the sums to obtain the weighted finite-difference transform
proof_steps.body_md: Disjointness of $T,E$ gives $\Delta_Tg(S)=\sum_{U\subseteq S}w_{T\cup U}$. Every pair $U\subseteq S\subseteq E$ occurs exactly once, so exchange the finite sums. For fixed $U$, the preceding superset-weight identity supplies precisely the displayed coefficient of $w_{T\cup U}$.

definitions.body_md: Fix a finite universe $N$. A game $g:\mathcal P(N)\to\mathbb R$ has output baseline $b=g(\varnothing)$ and interaction $I_g(A)=\sum_{U\subseteq A}(-1)^{|A|-|U|}g(U)$. Sum weights over all supersets of a fixed subset

Apply the shared identity at the top order

en.title: Complete shared proof: zero classical mixed partials and rectangular differences
en.overview: Globally zero classical mixed partials give zero rectangular differences. The actual coordinate-mask alternating sum is that difference; nonempty centering then recovers the original interaction.
assumptions: The original C1-function setting is retained. Global high-order mixed partials in 1-β are interpreted as classical existing derivatives; required prefix differentiability unfolds their definition and is not replaced by a total Lean deriv function returning zero.
All masks use the same fixed input baseline r and M∈ℕ. No analyticity, infinite Taylor representation, or polynomial premise is added.

definitions.body_md: Fix $N=\{1,\ldots,n\}$, $v:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$, x, and r. The coordinate mask keeps x_i on A and r_i elsewhere. Let $g(A)=v(x_A)$, $b=g(\varnothing)$, and $g_0(A)=g(A)-b$. The source interaction is $I(A)=I_{g_0}(A)$, with empty value zero. Let e_i be the coordinate unit vector and $a_i=x_i-r_i$ the actual masking increment.

proof_steps.title: Classical mixed partials and their existence order
proof_steps.body_md: The classical partial is $D_i f(z)=\left.\frac d{dt}f(z+t e_i)\right|_{t=0}$. Encode a multiindex by a nondecreasing coordinate list $(i_1,\ldots,i_q)$, and define $P_0=v$, $P_j=D_{i_j}P_{j-1}$. Classical existence of the stated mixed partials includes actual differentiability of each required prefix along the next coordinate, and 1-β gives $P_q\equiv0$. These existence conditions and the zero value are encoded together; only lists q>M are used. No extra global smoothness of all low derivatives is assumed. C1 alone does not imply existence of high derivatives. A fixed ascending order is used; a reverse convention can use the same difference argument in reverse order, without interchanging mixed partials.

proof_steps.body_md: Define $\delta_{a,i}f(z)=f(z+a e_i)-f(z)$. If f is differentiable along coordinate i everywhere, its finitely many translated sums and differences are too. Translation gives $D_i(f(\cdot+h))(z)=D_i f(z+h)$ because $(z+t e_i)+h=(z+h)+t e_i$. The one-variable difference rule yields $D_i(\delta_{a,j}f)=\delta_{a,j}(D_i f)$. Induction extends this to arbitrary finite rectangular differences. Only translations and finite additions are used, with no infinite series or higher directional chain rule.

For the empty list, both the difference and the order-zero partial are f, and its assumed zero value proves the claim. For a nonempty list, let R denote the remaining differences. The prefix-existence premise applies the induction hypothesis to $D_{i_1}f$, giving $R(D_{i_1}f)=0$. Commutation then gives $D_{i_1}(Rf)=0$. en.title: Shared proof: exact reconstruction by the OR complement transform
assumptions: $T\subseteq N$; $g:\mathcal P(N)\to\mathbb R$. Nonempty OR dividends are the negative AND transform of the complement game; the empty OR dividend is the original output baseline.

definitions.body_md: Fix a finite universe $N$. A game $g:\mathcal P(N)\to\mathbb R$ has output baseline $b=g(\varnothing)$ and interaction $I_g(A)=\sum_{U\subseteq A}(-1)^{|A|-|U|}g(U)$. Write $w_A=I_g(A)$. Every subset sum includes the empty set, and $w_\varnothing=b$. The finite difference is $\Delta_Tg(S)=\sum_{L\subseteq T}(-1)^{|T|-|L|}g(L\cup S)$. No zero output baseline is assumed. Centering $g_0=g-b$ removes only the empty dividend. For nonempty targets, $O_g^N(S)=-I_{g^c}(S)$ where $g^c(L)=g(N\setminus L)$; the empty OR coefficient is $g(\varnothing)$.

proof_steps.title: Intersecting subsets are a difference of two powersets
proof_steps.body_md: For $T\subseteq N$ and $S\subseteq N$, disjointness from $T$ is equivalent to $S\subseteq N\setminus T$. Therefore the intersecting family is $\mathcal P(N)\setminus\mathcal P(N\setminus T)$. The second powerset is contained in the first, so its sum is subtracted from the full sum. The empty set belongs to both full families and to neither intersecting family.

proof_steps.title: Reconstruct the negative complement game twice
proof_steps.body_md: Let $f(L)=-h(N\setminus L)$. Linearity shows that each nonempty OR coefficient equals $I_f(S)$. Every intersecting set is nonempty, so substitute these coefficients throughout the intersecting sum. Apply reconstruction on $N$ and on $N\setminus T$ to obtain $f(N)-f(N\setminus T)=-h(\varnothing)+h(T)$. The final complement equality uses the checked premise $T\subseteq N$.

proof_steps.title: Add back the separately defined empty OR baseline
proof_steps.body_md: The empty OR coefficient is $h(\varnothing)=v_{or}(x_\varnothing)$. Adding it to the intersecting sum gives $v_{or}(x_T)$. For empty $T$, the intersecting family is empty and only the baseline remains; for $T=N$, the full output is recovered. This also avoids double-counting source cases when $T$ is empty.

empty_set.text_md: 所有子集求和均包含空集，除非明确写成非空子集。
